ai.description: This 1.5m sea snake has a yellowish body with 50–70 black crossbands. It features a compressed, paddle-like tail and a distinctively small head relative to its robust, elongated body.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the presence of 50–70 distinct black bands that narrow significantly on the flanks, combined with a yellow-tinged body and a distinctively compressed tail.
ai.habitat: *Hydrophis cyanocinctus* inhabits shallow coastal waters, estuaries, and mangrove swamps across the Indian subcontinent, typically remaining at sea-level depths.
ai.behavior: The annulated sea snake is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for eels and gobies along the seafloor by probing crevices with its sensitive, fork-like tongue.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hydrophis cyanocinctus* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to live young. They typically produce litters of 3–16 offspring, with breeding occurring between May and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Annulated Sea Snake occurs along the entire coastline of the Indian subcontinent, from Pakistan through India to Bangladesh, inhabiting shallow coastal waters.
